header:
Date: 2027-07-22
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Alicia Chen (Redwood AE), Mark Duarte (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Cygnus - Head of Security), Tom Everett (CTO), Liam Shaw (DevOps)
Meeting purpose: Initial security posture discovery for evaluation of Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment options
summary: Cygnus Health is evaluating Redwood for a patient-facing NLP routing and summarization feature. Primary concerns are SOC 2/ISO attestations, SSO/SAML and SCIM for provisioning, RBAC and audit log retention, KMS/HSM encryption and key custody, data residency, and retention policies. Cygnus prefers Hosted for speed to market but needs clarity on encryption at rest & in transit, separation of logs, and ability to move to Dedicated or Private for certain sensitive workloads. Next steps: Redwood to send SOC2 and architecture docs; schedule technical deep dive and provide VPC peering checklist and retention artifact.
topics: Encryption, KMS, HSM and key custody
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment tradeoffs
Networking / VPC peering and egress considerations
transcript:
[00:00] Alicia: Hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm alicia with Redwood, i'll kick it off. quick roll call please.
[00:08] Priya: Hi, priya nair here, head of security at cygnus.
[00:11] Tom: Tom everett, cto.
[00:13] Liam: Liam shaw, devops.
[00:15] Mark: Mark duarte, solutions engineer, happy to dig into the tech.
[00:18] Alicia: Great, thanks. Objective for today is to understand your security requirements for hosted vs dedicated vs private, and what would unblock a pilot.
[00:26] Priya: Yep, main things for us are SOC2 type two, hopefully iso27001 as well, sso with saml and scim for provisioning, fine grained rbac, audit logs with long retention for investigations, and encryption key custody - we have strict rules around keys for patient data.
[00:42] Tom: Also data residency - some PHI-backed workloads need to remain in our VPC or in-region only.
[00:47] Mark: Makes sense. On the compliance side redwood's hosted offering is SOC2 type II, we maintain ISO attestation for the platform - i'll follow up with the exact certs and the report. For hosted customers we encrypt data in transit with TLS and at rest using envelope encryption; keys are managed in our KMS. For dedicated/private we can support customer-managed keys via KMS integrations or HSM for on-prem.
[01:10] Priya: When you say customer-managed keys, do you mean key custody is entirely on our side? we need non-exportable keys for certain workloads.
[01:18] Mark: For private/on-prem we can support HSM-backed keys where Redwood never holds the root key. For Dedicated we offer a BYOK flow where the customer rotates keys in their KMS and we call the key via a secure gateway - the root material stays in your tenant KMS, non-exportable. For Hosted we also have envelope keys but we can put a key under your control in many cases depending on the contract - i'll include the exact threat model in the doc.
[01:44] Liam: How about audit logs and retention? we need 18 months for some regs, and immutable logs would be ideal.
[01:50] Alicia: Good callout. Mark?
[01:52] Mark: Audit logs are stored in our logging pipeline, we provide rbac controlled access and can export to your splunk or datadog. Retention for hosted by default is 90 days but we have add-ons for extended retention and exports; for Dedicated/Private you control retention windows and can ship logs to your S3 or SIEM. Immutability can be achieved via write-once S3 policies in your account for Dedicated/Private.
[02:12] Priya: That's promising. For sso we use okta, need SAML 2.0 + SCIM for provisioning, and want to validate roles mapping for least-privilege.
[02:21] Mark: Redwood supports SAML 2.0 SSO and SCIM for provisioning. We map SCIM groups to RBAC roles; you can define custom roles and least-privilege policies. For audit we log changes to role bindings and provisioning events.
[02:33] Tom: How deterministic is performance? we have a UX SLO of 500ms for inference tail latency on 90th percentile for the patient routing service. We're trying to weigh the cost/perf tradeoffs between hosted and dedicated.
[02:44] Alicia: Right, that's more of an infra question, Mark can speak to throughput and SLA.
[02:48] Mark: For Hosted we publish performance profiles per model and region; dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools for predictable tail latency. We can instrument and run a pilot to measure 90p latency with your payloads - often customers start hosted for dev and move critical workloads to Dedicated/Private. Note that batching and KV caching affect tail latency.
[03:07] Priya: Back to security, what about multi-tenant separation? we want to ensure logs or memory can't cross tenants.
[03:13] Mark: Our runtime enforces tenant isolation; for hosted we use strong multi-tenant isolation boundaries in the control plane and per-tenant runtime namespaces. For dedicated you get isolated GPU pools and private networking. We'll include the architecture diagram showing control plane vs data plane separation.
[03:29] Liam: Are there network egress costs or data exfil protections? we need to control outbound traffic from inference nodes.
[03:34] Mark: Yes, for Dedicated and Private you can restrict egress via VPC/firewall rules. For Hosted we have egress filtering options and can disable outbound internet for specific routes; we'll include the egress policy document.
[03:47] Priya: Can we get longer retention for prompt logs but redact PII automatically?
[03:52] Mark: We provide configurable retention and redaction hooks - you can configure automatic redaction rules or tokenize before sending. For higher compliance we recommend private deployment or shipping logs to your own SIEM so you retain control.
[04:05] Tom: On legal side, do you provide data processing agreements and BAA for health data?
[04:09] Alicia: We have standard DPA and can sign BAAs for covered entities - i'll confirm the exact language and send the template.
[04:16] Priya: Okay good. another concern: model weights and artifacts - do you persist model-generated outputs and for how long?
[04:23] Mark: By default we keep logs for the configured retention window; model artifacts are versioned in our model catalog but inference outputs are treated as logs. You can configure zero-retention for outputs or have them routed to your storage. We'll show the policy table.
[04:36] Liam: If we do private on-prem, what's the install footprint and operational burden? we try to avoid heavy ops.
[04:41] Mark: Our private package is containerized with an operator; it can run on k8s or a managed cluster. We offer an install engineer as part of enterprise packages and can do a turn-key deployment with minimal ops from your team. For Dedicated we manage the infra and you get the benefits with less ops.
[04:57] Priya: Are there third-party pen tests or vuln scanning you do regularly?
[05:01] Mark: Yes, quarterly vuln scans and annual pen tests; we provide executive summaries and remediation timelines. We'll include recent pen test redactions as part of the pack.
[05:10] Tom: For SAML and SCIM mapping, can we limit provisioning to certain groups and separate admin roles from developer roles?
[05:17] Mark: Absolutely. SCIM lets you map Okta groups to custom RBAC roles; admin role separation is supported and we log role elevation requests.
[05:25] Priya: About encryption, is data encrypted at rest in backups and snapshots too?
[05:29] Mark: Yes, snapshots and backups are encrypted and follow the same KMS envelope policies. For Dedicated, backups can be stored in your account under your KMS.
[05:36] Liam: What about key rotation cadence and zero-downtime rotations?
[05:40] Mark: We support key rotation with seamless envelope key handover; for BYOK we coordinate rotation with your KMS and provide docs for zero-downtime rotation procedures.
[05:50] Priya: Any limitations on tokenization/PII redaction performance impact? we can't add huge latency.
[05:56] Mark: Tokenization can be done pre-ingest in your pipeline to avoid inference latency. If redaction occurs as a post-processing step it's async. We can bench both approaches in the pilot.
[06:07] Alicia: quick pause — any other compliance frameworks?
[06:10] Priya: We may need ISO 27701 guidance and specifics around HIPAA controls.
[06:15] Mark: Noted — we'll include HIPAA mapping and ISO 27701 considerations in the doc pack.
[06:21] Tom: On cost, if we move some workloads to Dedicated, what's the commitment model?
[06:25] Alicia: Dedicated is reserved capacity with monthly or annual commitments, and options for burst capacity. We'll include a ballpark pricing sheet.
[06:32] Priya: One more: can we run audits with names/ids of admin actions? we need non-reputable logs and exported chain of custody.
[06:40] Mark: We provide cryptographic log signing and exportable audit trails for Dedicated/Private; hosted customers can export logs to their SIEM where the chain of custody can be established.
[06:51] Liam: For the pilot, we want a small POC where we route a subset of traffic to Redwood hosted and measure latency and logs. If successful we may scope a Dedicated POC.
[06:59] Alicia: Sounds good. we'll do a pilot plan — mark, can you lead the tech run and provide the steps?
[07:04] Mark: Yep, i'll draft the POC runbook: test payloads, perf scripts, endpoint configs, and network steps. I'll also include the VPC peering checklist for the Dedicated option.
[07:14] Priya: We'll need to involve our legal/compliance folks — tom will share contacts.
[07:18] Tom: yes i'll loop them in.
[07:21] [cross talk] Alicia: ok great, recap — Alicia to send SOC2/ISO and DPA/BAA template; Mark to send network and key management docs plus POC runbook; customer to confirm retention and reviewers and to schedule the technical deep dive. Anything else?
[07:36] Priya: Please include example RBAC role definitions and a sample audit export format.
[07:40] Mark: noted.
[07:43] Liam: Also include SAML/SCIM quickstart for okta.
[07:46] Alicia: We'll get all that over. thanks everyone.
[07:50] Tom: Thanks. bye.
[07:52] [call ends]
